response.sql: WITH rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost, CAST(AVG(rental_rate) AS DOUBLE) / AVG(rental_duration) AS daily_price FROM film GROUP BY rating), cross_avg AS (SELECT AVG(daily_price) AS avg_daily_price FROM rating_stats), kept AS (SELECT rs.avg_replacement_cost, rs.daily_price, ca.avg_daily_price AS threshold FROM rating_stats rs CROSS JOIN cross_avg ca WHERE rs.daily_price > ca.avg_daily_price) SELECT AVG(avg_replacement_cost) AS avg_of_avg_replacement_cost, AVG(daily_price) AS avg_daily_price, AVG(daily_price - threshold) AS avg_excess_over_cross_avg FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: Each rating's average rental_rate and average rental_duration are plain AVG over all films in that rating, and daily price is their ratio (ratio of averages, as the request specifies), not an average of per-film daily prices.
The cross-rating average is the simple mean of the five ratings' daily prices, each rating weighted equally, as the request states.
Average replacement cost is taken over films (one row per film), not over inventory copies.
The division is done in DOUBLE to avoid MySQL's DECIMAL division truncating digits, so the result is not rounded. This is a precision choice, not a change in meaning.
